blind_spots.blind_spot: The site's only use of 'deployment' refers to manufacturing/unit cost scale ('practical cost for large-scale deployment'), never to fielded operating conditions -- despite defense applications listed for Robotic Combat Vehicle autonomy that would need onboard tuning without home-station connectivity.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A radar OS processing pipeline tuned for lab/road conditions and marketed on cost-at-scale, not on operating in a contested/DDIL environment, risks the same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case once it's mounted on an actual combat vehicle instead of a test car.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company is automotive-ADAS-first commercially (ADAS press releases dominate the news section) and has not yet had a defense fielding event force the redesign.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "HROS...delivers unmatched clarity and responsiveness at a practical cost for large-scale deployment"

blind_spots.blind_spot: Zero ITAR/export-control language anywhere despite RTX Ventures as a strategic investor and defense applications explicitly including Counter-UAS and ECCM (electronic counter-countermeasures) -- technology categories that are textbook ITAR-controlled.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Selling the same branded radar OS into commercial automotive customers and DoD ECCM/Counter-UAS programs with no visible IP or data segregation is the kind of thing that stalls a defense contract in legal/export review long after the engineering is done.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Dual-use go-to-market (GM Ventures + RTX Ventures both on the cap table) suggests the company hasn't yet had to formally separate its commercial and defense-controlled technology stacks.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Defense use cases (Surface-to-Air, Air-to-Air, Autonomy/Robotic Combat Vehicle) are listed as marketing bullets identical in tone to the automotive ADAS bullets, with no separate SWaP-C, training, or sustainment story for a vehicle-mounted radar operating in dust/heat/vibration versus a passenger-car sensor suite.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Combat-vehicle SWaP-C constraints (power budget, thermal, ruggedization, battle-damage sparing) are materially different from automotive OEM constraints; reusing the same spec sheet risks a hardware redesign the company hasn't budgeted for.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The product roadmap and messaging are still anchored to the larger, better-funded automotive ADAS market (RTX and GM Ventures both cited primarily around automotive safety in the news section).

opener_hook: NPS's Army Phase II SBIR targets multiband radar for autonomous military vehicles -- is HROS's software stack ITAR-segregated yet from the ADAS commercial build?
what_they_do: Builds AI-powered, patented software-defined radar (HROS/AtomicSense) for high-resolution perception, sold dual-use into automotive ADAS and defense sensing/autonomy applications.
